meta_description:
743 likes, 400 comments - rohitjoshi.ig on August 19, 2026: "Credit card arbitrage is basically using the interest-free credit period of a card to temporarily deploy your own cash elsewhere.

For example: You spend ₹1 lakh on a credit card, keep your ₹1 lakh in a liquid/short-term instrument during the billing cycle, and repay the card in full before the due date. The return earned during that period becomes your arbitrage gain.

The key is: no interest, no late fees, and no unnecessary transaction charges—otherwise the arbitrage can quickly disappear.".
